summary: Three Rentals at one price, none of them holding the 2GB image, so nothing but what each machine published about its own link can decide the placement. The first published 750 Mbps to the registry and stands behind it, stating nine tenths of a point of confidence. The second published 5 Gbps and disowned it, stating zero: a publisher that puts no confidence in its own number has measured nothing, and Mercator reads that as the silence it is rather than as the fastest machine in the fleet. The third published nothing at all. The two that said nothing worth acting on are charged the standing assumption, 500 Mbps at half a point of confidence, and they are identical: the disowned answer buys its publisher exactly what saying nothing buys. Before this rule a confidence of zero was dropped from the record instead of read as a disowned answer, so the disowned machine was charged 3.7 seconds it never justified and no doubt at all, and it won every time.
